■ Bank XXX Call Centre Officer Reference Guide — 
Payments & Transfer Services (Revised) 
This guide provides call centre officers with practical advice on how to handle customer 
enquiries about payments and transfers in Bank XXX’s mobile banking app. It focuses on 
what to be aware of, how to respond, and how to maintain customer trust while ensuring 
fraud prevention.

Transaction Limits 
When a transfer fails or cannot be completed, officers should first check whether the 
customer has reached their daily or per-transaction limit. 
If the transaction limit has been hit, the issue is that the transfer amount exceeds the 
current limit. The appropriate plan is to guide the customer to either increase their limit or 
reduce the transac

either increase their limit or 
reduce the transaction amount. 
If the customer has recently increased their transaction limit, the issue is that the new limit 
is not yet active because of the 12-hour cooling period that applies for security reasons. 
During this time, transactions above the previous limit will still be blocked. The best plan is 
to advise the customer to wait until the cooling p

to advise the customer to wait until the cooling period ends, or, if the transaction is urgent, 
to make smaller transfers within the old limit until the new one takes effect. Reassure the 
customer that this waiting period is a deliberate safety feature, not a system fault. 
 
Adding or Managing Payees 
 
Customers must have a registered payee for any transaction above $1,000. 
If the customer tr

any transaction above $1,000. 
If the customer tries to transfer more than $1,000 without a payee, the issue is that no 
payee has been set up for that amount. The plan is to either add a new payee or complete 
a smaller transfer under $1,000, which does not require a payee. 
If the customer recently added a new payee, the issue is likely that the payee is still within 
the 12-hour activation (co

payee is still within 
the 12-hour activation (cooling) period before funds can be sent. This restriction prevents 
fraudsters from adding unauthorized recipients. The plan is to wait until the cooling period 
ends, or, if the payment is urgent, to send a smaller amount under $1,000 that does not 
require a payee. 
 
Transfers and Scheduled Payments 
If a customer says their transfer didn’t go th

ts 
If a customer says their transfer didn’t go through: first check whether the transfer was 
scheduled for a future date or saved as a draft. Confirm if step-up verification (digital token 
or OTP) was completed. Transfers can also be held for internal fraud review if patterns 
appear unusual. Avoid giving technical details — instead say: 'Sometimes our system 

performs a quick safety check bef

mes our system 

performs a quick safety check before confirming certain transactions. It will go through 
automatically once cleared.' Encourage customers to always check confirmation 
messages or email receipts before assuming failure. 
 
 
Overseas and Cross-Border Payments 
Be aware that exchange rates for cross-border or QR payments are indicative and can 
refresh before confirmation. Some cr

tive and can 
refresh before confirmation. Some cross-border schemes have daily limits (for example, 
PromptPay Thailand » S$1,000/day). If a customer mentions 'rate expired' or 'payment 
failed,' suggest they refresh or retry later. Remind them never to share screenshots or QR 
codes that show account information. 
 
 
PayNow and QR Code Use 
Remind customers that linking their NRIC/FIN or mobile

nd customers that linking their NRIC/FIN or mobile number directs incoming funds to 
the selected account. Ensure they always review recipient details carefully before 
confirming a payment. For receiving money, QR codes must be generated from the official 
Bank XXX app. If customers are asked to scan a code from an unknown source, advise 
them not to proceed and report potential scams.

Bill Payments and Non-Bank Transfers 
If a bill payment fails, first verify the biller name and reference number. Wrong reference 
numbers may post to another account. For fintech wallets or NFIs, explain that minor 
delays can happen due to partner processing. Never promise instant reversals — record 
the transaction reference, inform the customer of t

he transaction reference, inform the customer of the review process, and escalate as 
required. 
 
 
Electronic Deferred Payments (EDP / EDP+) 
EDP transactions are typically used by corporate or high-value customers. Always clarify 
whether the caller is the issuer or recipient — this determines what actions they can take. 
Advise them to review payment details carefully before confirming, cancel

ayment details carefully before confirming, cancelling, or rejecting, 
as these are legally binding. 
 
 
Documentation and After-Call Notes 
Record the exact issue and the verification steps completed, Good notes ensure 
smooth handovers if follow-up is needed.

Bank XXX Call Centre Officer Guide — Fraud
Awareness and Response
Context: Why Fraud Awareness Matters
Fraud prevention has become one of the most critical responsibilities for frontline officers at Bank
XXX. In recent years, scams have evolved from simple phishing messages into highly coordinated,
emotionally manipulative schemes that exploit customer trust and urgency. Fraudsters now
impersonate

omer trust and urgency. Fraudsters now
impersonate not only bank employees but also government agencies, delivery services, and even
law enforcement, often using official logos, spoofed numbers, and convincing language to appear
legitimate. Customers typically contact the bank after they have unknowingly authorized a
transaction — believing they were securing their accounts, paying legitimate bill

re securing their accounts, paying legitimate bills, or complying with
instructions from someone claiming authority. Because many of these scams rely on social
engineering rather than hacking, victims are often unaware that they have been manipulated until
the funds have left their accounts. Call centre officers are, therefore, the first line of defense in
detecting and responding to fraud. Their

fense in
detecting and responding to fraud. Their ability to identify red flags during a call — such as unusual
behavior, nervous tone, external coaching, or repeated limit changes — can stop financial losses in
progress. An empathetic and structured response also helps rebuild customer trust in the bank,
ensuring that customers feel supported rather than blamed. Effective fraud response combines

er than blamed. Effective fraud response combines
three key elements: Speed, Accuracy, and Empathy. Acting quickly to freeze or block accounts
reduces potential exposure. Gathering detailed, factual information supports investigations.
Reassuring affected customers with calm, professional communication ensures confidence in the
bank’s systems and care. Officers must be equipped not only with syste

are. Officers must be equipped not only with system knowledge but also with
psychological awareness — understanding how scammers manipulate emotions like fear, urgency,
or authority. By maintaining composure, following procedures, and educating customers, call centre
staff play a direct role in protecting lives and livelihoods from financial harm.
How Fraud Is Detected
Bank XXX’s fraud detection s

How Fraud Is Detected
Bank XXX’s fraud detection systems use a combination of transaction pattern analysis, device
fingerprinting, behavioral monitoring, and customer reporting to identify possible fraud. Red flags
may include unusually large or urgent transfers, transactions to new payees added recently,
multiple limit changes in a short period, or transfers following a suspicious phone call or m

r transfers following a suspicious phone call or message. If
any of these indicators appear, officers should act immediately to secure the customer’s account.
Responding to Suspected Fraud – 4 Key Steps
Step 1 – Verify the Fraudulent Transaction and Secure the Account
Once the customer reports a suspicious or unauthorized transaction, calmly confirm the details —
the amount, time, payee, and chann

m the details —
the amount, time, payee, and channel used. Secure all related accounts immediately by freezing
access, blocking cards, or disabling digital services. If available, guide the customer to trigger the
Kill Switch or equivalent emergency lock function.
Step 2 – Protect Customer Information and Contain Exposure

Assist the customer in changing passwords, disabling compromised devices, a

anging passwords, disabling compromised devices, and reviewing linked
services. Ensure no further unauthorized logins can occur. Document all containment measures
clearly in the internal system.
Step 3 – Advise the Customer to Lodge a Police Report and Escalate Internally
Explain that filing a police report is essential for formal investigation and possible recovery. Provide
clear guidance on how

possible recovery. Provide
clear guidance on how and where to file — for example, via the SPF e-services portal or at the
nearest police post. Immediately escalate the case to the bank’s fraud operations team with all
relevant details attached.
Step 4 – Reassure and Educate
Once the account is secured and escalation completed, reassure the customer that the incident will
be reviewed thoroughly by

r that the incident will
be reviewed thoroughly by the fraud team. Advise them on safe banking habits, such as not sharing
OTPs, verifying caller identities, and avoiding third-party remote access tools. Emphasize that all
follow-ups will come only from official Bank XXX channels.
Key Message
Fraud response is not only about stopping transactions — it is about preserving trust. Every officer
must

it is about preserving trust. Every officer
must act swiftly, verify carefully, and communicate compassionately. A structured, calm, and
empathetic approach reassures victims, supports investigations, and strengthens public confidence
in Bank XXX’s commitment to safety.

How to manage your limits
Step 1 : Login to UOB TMRW and tap “Transaction limits". Step 2 : Select the limit you wish to change. Step 3 : Your current and new limit will be shown here. Step 4 : Review your new limit and swipe right to confirm. As a fraud control measure, there is a 12h cooling period before your limit increase takes effect. This does not apply for limit reductions. Step 5 : Next,

es not apply for limit reductions. Step 5 : Next, enter your digital token code as an added layer of security. This step is not required for limit reductions. Step 6 : Your change of transaction limit is successful.

How to add a payee
Step 1 : Login to UOB TMRW and tap “Pay & Transfer". Step 2 : Tap on "Add Payee or Biller" at the bottom of the screen. Step 3 : Select the funds transfer proxy type from the dropdown list. Step 4 : Review your recipient details by swiping to the right. Step 5 : As an added layer of security, you will be required to enter your digital token code to proceed. Step 6 : You will rec

gital token code to proceed. Step 6 : You will receive an SMS notification, confirming of your newly added payee. As a fraud control measure, there is a 12h cooling period before your new payee is added. This does not apply for payee removals.

How to perform a funds transfer
Step 1 : Login to UOB TMRW and tap “Pay & Transfer". Step 2 : Tap on “My Accounts/ Cards“  if it is a transfer to your own account. Alternatively, you can tap on "Other Accounts/ Cards“ for transfer to other accounts. Step 3 : Select the bank account to transfer to. Step 4 : The debiting account will be pre-selected from your last transaction. Enter the amount and d

from your last transaction. Enter the amount and date of transfer. Tap "Next" to proceed. Step 5 : In the confirmation screen, review the details and swipe right to confirm. Step 6 : You have successfully performed a funds transfer.

How to perform a scheduled transfer
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and tap on "Pay & Transfer". Step 2 : Tap on the Account you wish to pay or transfer the fund to. Step 3 : Input the amount you are transferring to. Next, tap on the calendar icon to select the date for the first fund transfer to be initiated. Step 4 : To setup a recurring fund transfer, you will need to select a future dated date. If

r, you will need to select a future dated date. If you select "Today" as the date of transfer, it will be treated as a one off immediate fund transfer. Step 5 : Select the frequency of the recurring fund transfer (e.g. Once, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly). Step 6 : Select the number of times you wish for the recurring fund transfer to take place You can select from 1 to 24, or "Indefinite" if

e You can select from 1 to 24, or "Indefinite" if there is no end date for this recurring fund transfer. Step 7 : You will be prompted to confirm that the transfer is to be sent to a payee that you know and trust. Tap on "Continue" to proceed. Step 8 : In the confirmation screen, check all details and swipe right to confirm. Step 9 : The recurring fund transfer setup is completed.

Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and select "Scan to pay". Step 2 : Scan the QR code or upload it from your device. Step 3 : The merchant details will be populated. Fill in the transaction amount in the local currency. An indicative exchange rate will be displayed. Click “Next” to proceed. Step 4 : Review and confirm the payment details. he payment details. Step 5 : Click ‘Share’ to generate an image that shows the successful payment without your account details. It can be saved or shared with the merchant.

How to Register and Pay with PayNow
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and tap "PayNow". Step 2 : Tap on "Setup". Step 3 : Input registration details. The PayNow name you have set will be shown to your sender. If you are the sender, your full name will be shown to the recipient. Step 4 : Select the Bank account you wish to link to your mobile number and/or NRIC/FIN. Step 5 : Successful registration. Step
r NRIC/FIN. Step 5 : Successful registration. Step 6 : You may now receive money in real-time securely and instantly via PayNow.

How to generate your PayNow QR code to receive money
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and select "Scan to pay". Step 2 : Tap on "My QR" and enter the amount you are requesting. Step 3 : Share your generated QR code with your friends to receive payment.

How to perform Scan to pay
Step 1 : Login to UOB TMRW and tap "Scan to pay". Step 2 : Select QR code or upload from device. Step 3 : Select Payment mode. Step 4 : Enter purchase amount. Step 5 : Select account. Step 6 : In the confirmation screen, check all details and swipe right to confirm. Step 7 : Successful transaction.

How to make a transfer via PayNow to VPA
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and select "PayNow". Step 2 : Tap on "VPA" and enter your Virtual Payment Address e.g. +6591234567#GRAB. Step 3 : Select the debiting account. Step 4 : Confirm your recipient details by swiping to the right. Step 5 : Transfer completed! Tap on "Share" to send an image of the transaction via your preferred social messaging app.

How to perform a funds transfer using Cash Advance
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and select "Pay/Transfer". Step 2 : Tap on "My UOB Accounts/Cards". Step 3 : Select the bank account to transfer to. Step 4 : Enter the amount and date of transfer. Tap "Next" to proceed. Step 5 : Click "Yes" to acknowledge and proceed with the Cash Advance transaction. Step 6 : In the confirmation screen, review the de
Step 6 : In the confirmation screen, review the details and swipe right to confirm. Step 7 : You have successfully performed a Cash Advance funds transfer.

How to send an EDP/EDP+
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW and tap “Pay & transfer". Step 2 : Tap on “Electronic Deferred Payment (EDP)”. Step 3 : Tap on “Issue new EDP”. Step 4 : Enter the details, select either EDP or EDP+ and tap on “Next”. Step 5 : Review the details and swipe right to confirm.

How to cancel an EDP
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW, tap “Services“ and “Manage EDP”. Step 2 : Tap on “Issued” and select EDP to cancel. Step 3 : Review EDP details and tap “Cancel payment”. Step 4 : Enter the reason for cancellation and tap “Next” Step 5 : Review and confirm details, then swipe right to confirm. Step 6 : EDP is cancelled. Tap “Share” to send details if needed.

How to collect an EDP/EDP+
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW, tap “Services“ and “Manage EDP”. Step 2 : Tap on “Received” and select EDP to collect payment on. Step 3 : Review EDP details and tap “Collect payment”. Step 4 : Review and confirm details, then swipe right to confirm. Step 5 : Your request to collect payment is submitted!

How to reject an EDP/EDP+
Step 1 : Log in to UOB TMRW, tap “Services“ and “Manage EDP”. Step 2 : Tap on “Received” and select EDP to reject. Step 3 : Review EDP details and tap “Reject payment”. Step 4 : Enter the reason for rejection and tap “Next” Step 5 : Review and confirm details, then swipe right to confirm. Step 6 : Your request to reject payment is submitted!
